newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures overcome a bout of early nerves to recoup a large proportion of Friday's losses and traders said the positive finish, which left the contract at the day's highs, provided a good platform for further gains.

The December contract tentatively pushed higher in the opening exchanges to set about filling a gap between 128.74 and 129.14 left on Friday. Traders said a late rally, partly driven by people taking new positions, left the contract at an intermediate resistance level of 128.94/96.
Traders said the rise on Monday was relatively cautious but there was every chance the gap would be closed on Tuesday.
French 10-year bonds held onto their relative gains of last week with the spread over German benchmark bonds remaining unchanged at minus six basis points.
Analysts said ongoing demand for French bonds from domestic investors, helped by coupon and redemptions of about 40 billion francs in December, provided support.
"As we saw on Friday, just below the surface there is pent up domestic demand," Iain Lindsay at Credit Lyonnais, said.
A trader at a French bank said Monday's rise was cautious and he thought prudence ahead of the year-end meant traders would be unlikely to go out on a limb with many new positions.
"I don't see a violent rebound. The day today showed the market is very cautious," he said. He said he thought the bond future would have difficult staying durably above 128.74/76.

Analysts said the main focus later this week, besides U.S. inflation figures, would be whether an agreement on a post-1999 budget discipline pact could be reached at the Dublin summit of European Union leaders.

"There's a logical difference between a monetary approach and a political approach (to European monetary union) and the stability pact is one of the key elements," Valerie Plagnol, market economist at Credit Commercial de France, said.

Analysts said while an agreement seemed quite likely, the terms of the stability pact would be the most important in determining the bond market reaction. The closer an agreement came to the original German proposals the better for French bonds, they said.
A delay in reaching an agreement might not be that disastrous as long as the negotiations did not descend into open conflict between member states at Dublin.
As expected, the Bank of France left the intervention rate unchanged at a regular money market tender on Monday and most economists expected rates to be left unchanged on Thursday.
